claims.title: Orbit cuts and exchange
claims.basis: Paths avoiding i stay in G_i-orbits; cutting both i-edges identifies the same two orbit classes.

claims.title: Selected square is a block
claims.basis: A selected external path uses neither square colour and closes a forbidden one-edge-colour cycle.

claims.title: Long-cycle reduction
claims.basis: One or two missing square edges suffice; new edges occur only on the new square, so long-cycle count decreases.

claims.title: Incident squares
claims.basis: Disjoint colour sets provide a commuting pair; any path to the new corner would enter both blocks from their common cut vertex.

claims.title: Ordinary transport
claims.basis: The surviving path or strict cycle decrease handles the first case; repeated connector colour forces an external new corner and three-component tree join.

claims.title: Global middle-colour exchange
claims.basis: Actual edges/eligibility survive the vertex permutation; the original square can be reinserted without any other new cycle; connector loses its first edge.

claims.title: Square normal form
claims.basis: Finite lexicographic minimization contradicts incident, ordinary or middle-colour transport; edge count yields2r<=n.

claims.title: Defect accounting
claims.basis: Delete one edge of each edge-disjoint square; connected components remain, yielding2r=n-c+q.

claims.title: Single crossing
claims.basis: The contracted orbit graph is connected with one edge; distant generators fix the two endpoints separately.

claims.title: No gap
claims.basis: Omitted-colour words split into commuting lower/upper intervals; endpoint movement contradicts the distant-generator fixed-point property.
